text:
sam: quick heads-up — saw growing resident memory for long-context runs on qwen-mqa. not immediate leak but KV pages keep accumulating and eviction doesn't bring RSS down. reproducer attached below. :eyes:

sam: minimal repro: run a 1k->32k token chat stream. after ~45m RSS climbs ~1.2GB and never drops despite evict counts increasing. logs: 
```
KV_EVICT count=4234 freed_pages=184 reclaimed=12 slab_frag=0.14
allocator: slab_total=8192MB used=7264MB free=928MB
runtime: kernel=fast_attn_quant fallback=kernel_v2
```

lia: is this only qwen-mqa or seen on qwen-gqa too?

sam: quick check says qwen-gqa doesn't show same steady drift, looks oscillatory instead. suspect MQA's packed KV layout interacts with rope-scaling alignment and our page-sweep heuristics.

devon: can you run with `--kv-trace=pages,evict --kv-compact=off` so we get raw page ids? might help see fragmentation pattern. also add `--kernel-profile` to see if kernel switches coincide with spikes.

sam: running now. command: `./bin/serve --model qwen-mqa --workload long-chat --kv-trace pages,evict --kernel-profile > /tmp/kvt.log &`

mira: if MQA packs KV differently, eviction granularity may be misaligned with slab size. we saw similar but smaller effect on mistral when rope scaling crosses 4096 boundaries. could be a slab boundary / kernel memory allocator interaction.

kevin: wondered if batching heuristics (continuous batching) keep stale KV refs alive. when batching window expands, a long-lived batch holds prefixes, preventing page reclamation. any chance the client is pinning prefixes?

sam: client-side pinning not in repro. I instrumented continuous-batcher and didn't see outstanding references after responses are returned. eviction counters go up but `reclaimed` stays low — suggests free pages are becoming non-contiguous so allocator can't merge.

tanvi: can we try enabling `kv_coalesce=true` on the fly? there is an experiment branch that runs a background coalesce sweep. might temporarily mitigate until we understand root cause.

sam: started a run with coalesce branch. early signs: reclaimed jumped to ~320 but RSS only dropped ~200MB. fragmentation metric still ~0.27.

devon: share `kvt.log` snippet? paste compressed sample if possible.

sam: pasted gist: https://redwood-internal/gists/kv-qwen-mqa-246802 — includes `heapmap` snapshots every 10m and kernel profile. notable: at ~00:42 kernel switches from `fast_attn_quant` -> `kernel_v2` right before a reclaim attempt.

lia: kernel switch could reorder memory access patterns, causing pages to be referenced differently and breaking LRU assumptions. can you add `--force-kernel=fast_attn_quant` to test?

sam: will do. also will run matching experiment for llama and mistral to compare rope scaling behavior.

mira: suggestion: add a synthetic test that walks long contexts but explicitly triggers different rope scales (e.g., 2048, 4096, 8192) and measure `evict_rate`, `fragmentation`, `coalesce_ops`. then we can correlate with kernel choice and MQA layout.

kevin: filed quick ticket INC-2026 and linked the trace. put a note to include `alloc-map` export for the next run.

tanvi: ops-bot: can you schedule a 2h dedicated-job on dynpool-12 with `--p99-slo=200ms` and the flags sam listed?

ops-bot: scheduled job `kv-drift-qwen-mqa-246802` on dynpool-12, 2h. link: https://infra/jobs/kv-drift-qwen-mqa-246802

sam: thanks. next steps: 1) forced-kernel run, 2) coalesce branch longer run, 3) cross-model sweep (llama/mistral/qwen) with synthetic rope-scale walker. I'll post perf diffs and a minimal repro script.

devon: if coalesce fixes, we should still root-cause allocator merge behavior. maybe adjust slab size or add a defragmentation pass that runs when free_pages / slab_threshold > X.

lia: +1. also add a perf counter to kernel-selection so we can correlate fallback events with fragmentation spikes in dashboards.

mira: will help with synthetic test harness tomorrow.

sam: ack. will update thread with results. :thumbsup:
